title: A $2,500 Zelle deposit for a real house that was never for rent

steps.label: Listing seen
steps.detail: A real house is listed for rent online. The owner still lives there and never offered it for rent.

steps.label: Asked to see it
steps.detail: The poster says the occupants will not move out for weeks and sends a link to a professional video tour instead of a viewing.

steps.label: Asked to pay to secure it
steps.detail: The renter is asked for an application fee and a security deposit to secure the house.

steps.label: Paid by Zelle
steps.detail: The renter pays a $75 application fee, then sends the $2,500 deposit by Zelle over several days, without ever seeing inside.

steps.label: Found out
steps.detail: The poster stops answering. The video tour had been copied from an older real estate listing.

findings.text: Taken in this home (3 of 3 photos).
Not checked (our data has no rent for this building).
No reply yet. An honest landlord may need time.
NOT SHOWN. Being inside does not mean they may rent it.
Zelle before a viewing. Red flag.

cant_catch: SNAPBACK does not open the video tour link, so it cannot tell that the tour was copied from an older listing. Real photos of a real house do not show that the poster may rent it.
